text:
Priya: handing off to @Mike — quick summary of the morning surge and what I did so you can pick up.

Priya: 03:15 UTC we started seeing ~30% 503s from serving-api in eu-west-1, p95 token latency jumped from ~120ms -> 1.2s.
Priya: incident-bot created pager at 03:18. paging window lasted ~40m with repeated flapping for a subset of Dedicated nodes. :warning:

incident-bot: AUTO PAGE: Serving 503 spike (eu-west-1) — escalation to eng-oncall. Links: https://status.redwood.local/incident/5620012345

Mike: got it, thanks. what looked like the root cause?

Priya: short version: GPU driver process OOMs on a small pool of Dedicated instances handling long-context batch requests. When those nodes dropped, smart-routing pushed traffic to the remaining pool and the smaller model variants; that caused batching backpressure and a crossover of CPU/GPU memory leading to transient OOMs + 503s.

Ashley: saw the same in logs — cluster-gpu-15 had repeated driver restarts. I also saw autoscaler spin up new nodes then immediately kill them due to node bootstrap script failing on a kernel preload step.

Priya: mitigation steps taken earlier:
- pinned traffic away from affected node pool (tag filter) to reduce blast radius.
- triggered rolling restart of the daemonset on the Dedicated pool (kube-cordon -> drain -> restart).
- temporarily lowered max-batch-size for eu-west routing policy to reduce memory pressure: `redwood route update --region eu-west-1 --max-batch-size 8`
- opened a support case with infra (ticket #INF-9482) for driver/kernel investigation.

Mike: nice. Any customer impact? which customers were affected?

Priya: roughly 12 customers had degraded responses for ~30–45m; two customers (internal names: alpha-co and docs-pro) reported truncated completions and timeouts. We alerted both via support with the temp mitigation and ETA. No data loss.

incident-bot: NOTE: runbook links added to incident: https://playbooks.redwood/internal/driver-oom and https://playbooks.redwood/internal/fallback-routing

Ashley: Observability notes:
- Prom alert: serving.p95_latency.eu-west1 > 900ms triggered repeatedly.
- Node metric: gpu.memory.used spiked to 98% on gpu-node-* before driver restart.
- Autoscaler events show repeated scale-up -> fail due to `bootstrap: kernel-preload` failing (exit 1).

Priya: current status at handoff (04:05 UTC):
- Primary mitigation stable: traffic pinned, p95 back to ~150–220ms.
- Affected nodes are cordoned and under investigation.
- Autoscaler fix pending infra response; we have a temporary manual pool available if autoscaling continues to fail.

Mike: ok. for the incoming shift: what are the immediate watch items?

Priya: watchlist for you — please check these in order:
1) Alerts: serving.503_rate.eu-west1 and serving.p95_latency.eu-west1. If either fires, escalate to infra on-call and consider re-routing traffic regional -> global fallback for affected customers.
2) Node health: `kubectl get nodes -l pool=dedicated-eu -o wide` and `kubectl describe node <node>` on any node with `Ready!=True`.
3) Autoscaler events: `kubectl -n infra logs deploy/autoscaler` and check for repeated `kernel-preload` failures. If autoscaler keeps failing, promote the manual standby pool: `infra pool promote manual-standby-eu`.
4) Customer impact: search for support tickets containing keywords `timeout`, `truncated` since 03:00 UTC; coordinate any account-level notices with Support.

Ashley: runbook quick commands (copy-paste):
```
# check recent driver restarts
kubectl -n serving logs -l app=gpu-driver --tail=200 | grep -E "oom|restart|panic"

# pin route away from pool
redwood route update --region eu-west-1 --exclude-pool dedicated-eu-1

# promote manual standby
infra pool promote manual-standby-eu --region eu-west-1
```

Priya: who is primary/secondary for the next 6 hours?

Mike: I'll take primary from 04:05 -> 10:05 UTC. Ashley will be secondary for the first 2 hours (04:05 -> 06:05) then rotate to oncall-rotation-bot’s scheduled secondary.

Priya: note coverage gap: we have limited human coverage in APAC overnight (00:00–06:00 UTC). If the autoscaler regresses, we may need to escalate to infra L2 and open a region-wide fallback. Oncall overlap suggestion: ask infra to stand by 05:00–07:00 UTC for eu-west kernel fix.

Mike: Ack. My immediate next steps: verify autoscaler logs, ensure manual pool promotion works, and confirm support notices sent to alpha-co and docs-pro.

Ashley: I'll validate logs and keep a watch on node restarts for the next hour. If I see repeated driver crashes, I'll open INF-EMER and ping infra-sig. :mag:

Priya: outstanding action items (owners):
- INF-9482: infra investigate kernel preload failure (Infra L2)
- Promote manual standby pool if autoscale fails (Mike)
- Confirm customer notices & update tickets (Support via Ashley)
- Postmortem owner assignment will be decided after infra's RCA — tentatively Priya + infra eng.

incident-bot: REMINDER: Did you attach the `driver-oom` runbook to the incident? If not, attach now.

Priya: attached. done.

Mike: thanks — will update this thread with any major changes before 06:00 UTC. If anything critical happens, I'll open a bridge and ping @here.

Ashley: small note — added a dashboard panel for eu-west long-context batch rate so we can correlate request shape with OOMs. link: https://dashboards.redwood.local/d/serving/eu-west-batches

Priya: handing off: good luck, and please escalate fast if autoscaler starts thrashing again. :pray:

Mike: taking over. primary: Mike, secondary: Ashley. coverage notes added to rotation calendar.

oncall-rotation-bot: Updated schedule: Mike primary 04:05-10:05 UTC, Ashley secondary 04:05-06:05 UTC.

Mike: (closing) leaving a short checklist pinned to the incident: monitor alerts, verify manual pool, confirm support contact. I'll add any follow-ups here.

Ashley: will post a short blameless summary when we have infra RCA.

Priya: passing off — thread ends, last checks green at 04:12 UTC.
